issues.description: In dd.py the ComputeTable.table attribute has inconsistent type annotations between the template and the solution. The template declares ComputeTable.table as a list of tuples (annotation: list[tuple[DD, DD, DDOperation, DD]]), but the implementation initializes it as a dictionary (self.table = {}) and the solution declares the attribute as a dict mapping (operand key) -> DD (annotation: dict[tuple[DD, DD, DDOperation], DD]). This mismatch in the template's type annotation vs. actual use (and vs. the solution) can confuse students reading the type hints, cause static type-checker warnings, and obscure the intended mapping semantics of the compute table.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's ComputeTable.table annotation to match the intended implementation and the solution: annotate it as a dict with tuple keys mapping to DD, e.g. table: dict[tuple[DD, DD, DDOperation], DD], and ensure the constructor initializes self.table = {}. This will align type hints with usage and the solution.
